phenomena.claim: Coupled irreversible flows exhibit reciprocal cross-coefficients in experiment (thermoelectric Seebeck/Peltier pairing, thermodiffusion, electrolyte transference)
phenomena.source: Stage-2 conversion target: Miller, Chem. Rev. 60, 15-37 (1960) ('Thermodynamics of Irreversible Processes: The Experimental Verification of the Onsager Reciprocal Relations') at abstract level
phenomena.caveat: the phenomenology (Thomson relations) predates the theory and is textbook-standard; the theoretical statement is carried VERIFIED under formalism (Onsager 1931)

phenomena.claim: KPZ universality is observed far from equilibrium: growing interfaces in nematic liquid-crystal electroconvection show self-affine roughening with the KPZ (1+1)-dimensional spatial and temporal scaling laws, and height-fluctuation statistics following random-matrix (largest-eigenvalue) distributions
phenomena.source: Takeuchi & Sano, Phys. Rev. Lett. 104, 230601 (2010) -- APS abstract fetched and verified 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: 1+1 dimensions; a single well-controlled experimental system class (topological-defect turbulence interfaces), since extended by the same group

phenomena.claim: Individual trajectories of a driven colloidal particle transiently consume entropy over colloidal length and time scales; the frequency of these entropy-consuming trajectories is quantified by the fluctuation theorem
phenomena.source: Wang, Sevick, Mittag, Searles & Evans, Phys. Rev. Lett. 89, 050601 (2002) -- APS abstract fetched and verified 2026-09-23
phenomena.caveat: 'violation' is trajectory-level only: the ensemble mean entropy production stays non-negative (see formalism); single-molecule work-relation experiments are recorded in the sibling statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics record (Collin et al. 2005), not duplicated here

phenomena.claim: Heat flows spontaneously from the colder to the hotter of two initially quantum-correlated qubits with the dynamics unchanged: reversal of the thermodynamic arrow at fixed dynamics, purchased by initial-state correlations and quantified as a trade-off between correlations and entropy
phenomena.source: Micadei, Peterson, Souza, Sarthour, Oliveira, Landi, Batalhao, Serra & Lutz, 'Reversing the direction of heat flow using quantum correlations', Nat. Commun. 10, 2456 (2019) -- verified 2026-09-23 via arXiv:1711.03323 abstract (journal reference confirmed there; nature.com page login-redirected)
phenomena.caveat: NMR two-spin implementation with effective spin temperatures; two qubits, not a macroscopic bath. This is the named O-converter for core item R9-2' (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 2.D(iii): dissipation direction is state-supplied while magnitude is dynamics-intrinsic) -- the observation displays the state-supplied direction directly; recorded here as bearing on that core item, with no requirement asserted (Stage 4's job)

formalism.claim: Kubo linear response theory: the first-order response of any observable to a perturbation is an equilibrium two-time correlation function of the unperturbed system (the Kubo formula), with applications to magnetic and conduction problems
formalism.source: Kubo, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 12, 570-586 (1957) -- Crossref metadata (author/title/journal/volume/pages/year) verified 2026-09-23; publisher page returned 403. The companion review Kubo, Rep. Prog. Phys. 29, 255 (1966) is carried VERIFIED in the sibling statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics record (FDT entry)
formalism.caveat: perturbative expansion around an equilibrium reference state; the FDT content of the same structure lives in the sibling record and is cross-referenced, not duplicated

formalism.claim: Green-Kubo transport relations: hydrodynamic transport coefficients (viscosity, thermal conductivity, diffusivity) are time integrals of equilibrium flux autocorrelation functions of the microscopic dynamics
formalism.source: Green, J. Chem. Phys. 22, 398-413 (1954) -- Crossref metadata verified 2026-09-23; Kubo, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 12, 570 (1957) as above
formalism.caveat: existence of the integrals presupposes sufficiently fast correlation decay -- see limits (long-time tails)

formalism.claim: Onsager reciprocity: the matrix of linear phenomenological coefficients coupling thermodynamic fluxes and forces is symmetric, L_ij = L_ji, derived from microscopic reversibility applied to the regression of fluctuations, expressible through a dissipation function
formalism.source: Onsager, Phys. Rev. 37, 405-426 (1931) ('Reciprocal Relations in Irreversible Processes. I.') -- APS abstract fetched and verified 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: linear near-equilibrium regime; Onsager's own recorded limitation: plain symmetry fails under magnetic fields or Coriolis forces (see symmetries for the field-reversal form)

formalism.claim: Mori-Zwanzig projection: projecting the microscopic dynamics onto a chosen set of slow variables yields an exact generalized Langevin equation -- systematic frequency term, memory-kernel convolution, and an orthogonal fluctuating force
formalism.source: Mori, Prog. Theor. Phys. 33, 423-455 (1965) ('Transport, Collective Motion, and Brownian Motion') -- Crossref metadata verified 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: exact but not by itself predictive: the kernel is defined through projected dynamics whose evaluation is generally as hard as the original problem. The operator-algebraic sibling (Nakajima-Zwanzig exact master equation with memory kernel) is carried VERIFIED in open_quantum_systems_decoherence (formalism) and is cross-referenced, not duplicated

formalism.claim: Stochastic thermodynamics: entropy production is defined along individual stochastic trajectories, and total entropy change (system + medium) obeys the integral fluctuation theorem <exp(-Delta s_tot)> = 1 for arbitrary initial states and time-dependent driving over finite times, whence <Delta s_tot> >= 0 by Jensen's inequality
formalism.source: Seifert, Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 040602 (2005) ('Entropy Production along a Stochastic Trajectory and an Integral Fluctuation Theorem') -- APS abstract fetched and verified 2026-09-23
formalism.caveat: declared dynamics classes: Langevin/master-equation stochastic dynamics; the Jarzynski/Crooks work relations from which this family grew are carried VERIFIED in the sibling statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics record (formalism), not duplicated here

primitives.claim: Local equilibrium (separation of time scales between fast microscopic relaxation and slow hydrodynamic variables) is a primitive of the hydrodynamic-level nonequilibrium description, assumed rather than derived
primitives.source: Stage-2 conversion target: de Groot & Mazur, Non-Equilibrium Thermodynamics (North-Holland, 1962), local-equilibrium postulate chapter, at citation level
primitives.caveat: textbook-standard framing; the corresponding microscopic-derivation absence is recorded under open_problems (Fourier's law)

primitives.claim: The choice of projection operator -- which variables count as slow/relevant -- is a declared input of the Mori-Zwanzig construction, not an output of it; different choices redistribute content between systematic, memory, and noise terms
primitives.source: structure of the formalism as introduced in Mori, Prog. Theor. Phys. 33, 423 (1965) (Crossref-verified 2026-09-23): the projector onto the chosen variable set is supplied at the outset
primitives.caveat: reading of the verified formalism, parallel to the system-environment-split primitive recorded in open_quantum_systems_decoherence (primitives); the two records' entries describe the same declared-decomposition pattern in different formalisms

derived_objects.claim: The fluctuation-dissipation relation of the second kind is derived within the Mori formalism: the memory kernel is fixed by the autocorrelation of the orthogonal fluctuating force, so dissipation (memory) and noise are two faces of one projected object
derived_objects.source: Mori, Prog. Theor. Phys. 33, 423-455 (1965) -- Crossref metadata verified 2026-09-23; kernel-noise relation is the paper's central structural result as standardly cited
derived_objects.caveat: abstract/metadata-level verification; equation-level correspondence flagged for Stage-2 full-text check. Equilibrium reference state assumed, matching the first-kind FDT scope in the sibling record

empirical_inputs.claim: Transport coefficients enter the hydrodynamic description as measured material inputs; Green-Kubo re-expresses them as equilibrium correlation functions of a declared microscopic model rather than deriving their values from new principles
empirical_inputs.source: Green, J. Chem. Phys. 22, 398 (1954); Kubo, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 12, 570 (1957) -- both Crossref-verified 2026-09-23
empirical_inputs.caveat: given a microscopic Hamiltonian the coefficients are computable in principle; the input character refers to the hydrodynamic level, where they are fitted

empirical_inputs.claim: In the tested small-system regime the direction of heat flow is supplied by initial-state data: with the dynamics fixed, preparing initial correlations reverses the flow
empirical_inputs.source: Micadei et al., Nat. Commun. 10, 2456 (2019) -- verified 2026-09-23 via arXiv:1711.03323 (see phenomena)
empirical_inputs.caveat: two-qubit NMR regime. This is the experimental face of the state-supplied-direction entries recorded in statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics (empirical_inputs, PROGRAM-RESULT) and bears on core item R9-2' (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 2.D(iii)) as its named O-converter; no requirement asserted here

constants.claim: Nonequilibrium statistical mechanics introduces no new fundamental constant: transport coefficients are material properties, and the fluctuation-theorem/linear-response structure uses only k_B (and hbar in quantum form), carried in the sibling records
constants.source: absence recorded against this record's verified formalism entries (Kubo, Green-Kubo, Onsager, Mori, Seifert structures introduce no constant beyond k_B, hbar, and model inputs); k_B entry lives in statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics (constants)
constants.caveat: KPZ-class exponents (e.g. beta = 1/3 in 1+1 D) are universal numbers, not fundamental constants; they are recorded under observables

symmetries.claim: Microscopic time-reversal symmetry (microscopic reversibility) is the input that yields reciprocity; under time-reversal-odd external fields the symmetry is restored only with field reversal, L_ij(B) = L_ji(-B)
symmetries.source: Onsager, Phys. Rev. 37, 405 (1931) -- APS abstract fetched 2026-09-23, including Onsager's own recorded breakdown under magnetic/Coriolis forces
symmetries.caveat: the field-reversal (Onsager-Casimir) completion is standard; its primary source (Casimir, Rev. Mod. Phys. 17, 343 (1945)) is named for Stage 2 rather than entered uncited. The Loschmidt-side content (microscopic reversibility vs macroscopic irreversibility) is carried in the sibling statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics record (symmetries)

limits.claim: Green-Kubo integrals exist only when flux correlations decay fast enough: hydrodynamic long-time tails (t^(-d/2)) make some transport coefficients divergent in low dimensions, bounding the domain of conventional hydrodynamic transport
limits.source: Stage-2 conversion target: Alder & Wainwright, Phys. Rev. A 1, 18 (1970) (velocity-autocorrelation long-time tails) at abstract level
limits.caveat: community-standard; entered TO-VERIFY because the citation is not yet checked

limits.claim: Onsager reciprocity and Green-Kubo response are recovered as the near-equilibrium linear expansion of the fluctuation-theorem structure (edge type LIMIT_RELATION)
limits.source: Stage-2 conversion targets: Gallavotti, Phys. Rev. Lett. 77, 4334 (1996) (Onsager reciprocity from the chaotic hypothesis); Lebowitz & Spohn, J. Stat. Phys. 95, 333 (1999) (Gallavotti-Cohen symmetry for stochastic dynamics, Green-Kubo recovery) at abstract level
limits.caveat: the sibling record's Jarzynski/Crooks entries are the far-from-equilibrium side of this limit; not load-bearing until converted

known_connections.claim: Kubo response evaluated on an equilibrium (KMS) state yields the fluctuation-dissipation theorem: the linear-response formalism's equilibrium input is exactly the FDT/KMS structure
known_connections.source: Kubo, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 12, 570 (1957) -- Crossref-verified 2026-09-23; the FDT and KMS entries themselves (Callen-Welton 1951; Kubo 1966; Pusz-Woronowicz passivity) are carried VERIFIED in statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics (formalism) and cross-referenced, not duplicated
known_connections.caveat: equilibrium reference state; for non-KMS baths see the sibling record's domain_of_validity NESS entry

known_connections.claim: PROGRAM machinery cross-reference: the archive's executable KMS admission gate tests (chi, noise) kernel pairs against the quantum FDT/KMS relation on a frequency grid, rejecting white-noise/temperature-independent kernels and T <= 0 -- the operational boundary between this domain's non-KMS bath classes and the equilibrium baseline
known_connections.source: archive ref: origin/v4:gate/kms.py (docstring, gate(), _self_test()); primary corpus entry in statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics (formalism)
known_connections.caveat: PROGRAM machinery note, not a physics claim: hbar = k_B = 1, bosonic Gaussian bath, tolerance-check implementation; in-house and unreviewed; recorded here only as the cross-domain pointer

known_connections.claim: PROGRAM cross-reference (gravity-side response/memory): the archive's certified T3 absorptive response -- one-loop graviton self-energy on de Sitter with fully certified non-analytic absorptive content through H^6 and stationarity/memory anti-correlated -- is the archive's gravity-side instance of the response-function/memory-kernel structure this domain formalizes
known_connections.source: archive ref: origin/physics-final:GRUT_FINAL_SYNTHESIS_01.md section 0 stopping statement and sections 1a-1c (T3 chain custody); the boundary entry itself is carried in open_quantum_systems_decoherence (known_connections) and is cross-referenced, not duplicated
known_connections.caveat: in-house, unreviewed; scoped to the certified nonanalytic absorptive sector only (not the complete self-energy; H^8 outside the certificate; u_b-dependent memory licensed only within the recorded deep-IR wall). Bears on core recurrence 5 (RRP_00_REQUIREMENTS_PICTURE_01 section 4: reference-state data carry asymmetries, laws carry magnitudes -- the T3 u_b-dependence and sign/magnitude split is its named program-side instance); no requirement asserted here

known_disconnects.claim: No general extremal principle governs far-from-equilibrium steady states: minimum-entropy-production characterizes only the linear near-equilibrium regime, and proposed maximum-entropy-production principles have no established general validity
known_disconnects.source: Stage-2 conversion target: Martyushev & Seleznev, Phys. Rep. 426, 1 (2006) (review, including scope limits) and the linear-regime restriction of Prigogine's minimum-entropy-production theorem, at abstract level
known_disconnects.caveat: recorded as a disconnect (variational principle does NOT extend beyond linear regime), community-standard but uncited as yet; not load-bearing

open_problems.claim: Derivation of Fourier's law and of hydrodynamics from microscopic Hamiltonian dynamics for generic interacting systems
open_problems.source: Stage-2 conversion target: Bonetto, Lebowitz & Rey-Bellet, 'Fourier's Law: a challenge for theorists', in Mathematical Physics 2000 (Imperial College Press), arXiv:math-ph/0002052, at abstract level
open_problems.caveat: the absence claim is community-standard; the named review is the check

open_problems.claim: Classification of far-from-equilibrium universality classes is incomplete; KPZ (1+1 D) is the established experimentally-anchored exception, not the rule
open_problems.source: Stage-2 conversion target: Takeuchi, 'An appetizer to modern developments on the Kardar-Parisi-Zhang universality class', Physica A 504, 77 (2018) at abstract level; the KPZ experimental anchor itself is VERIFIED under phenomena

observables.claim: Transport coefficients and thermoelectric cross-coefficients; interface roughness and growth exponents with height-fluctuation distributions (KPZ 1+1 D: beta = 1/3, random-matrix largest-eigenvalue statistics); trajectory-resolved work, heat, and entropy-production distributions
observables.source: Takeuchi & Sano, Phys. Rev. Lett. 104, 230601 (2010) (interface statistics); Wang et al., Phys. Rev. Lett. 89, 050601 (2002) (trajectory entropy production) -- both APS abstracts fetched 2026-09-23
observables.caveat: representative anchors, not an exhaustive itemization; equilibrium-side noise spectra and work distributions are recorded in the sibling statistical_mechanics_thermodynamics record (observables)

alternative_formulations.claim: Steady-state thermodynamics (SST): a proposed extension of thermodynamic structure (entropy, extended Clausius relations) to nonequilibrium steady states, phenomenologically framed by Oono-Paniconi and given a testable formulation by Sasa-Tasaki
alternative_formulations.source: Stage-2 conversion targets: Oono & Paniconi, Prog. Theor. Phys. Suppl. 130, 29 (1998); Sasa & Tasaki, J. Stat. Phys. 125, 125 (2006) at abstract level
alternative_formulations.caveat: a research program, not settled canon: whether SST closes into a complete NESS thermodynamics (unique nonequilibrium entropy/temperature) remains open; entered TO-VERIFY as permitted for this tranche

alternative_formulations.claim: Macroscopic fluctuation theory: a large-deviation formulation of driven diffusive systems in which NESS properties follow from a variational rate functional over density and current fields
alternative_formulations.source: Stage-2 conversion target: Bertini, De Sole, Gabrielli, Jona-Lasinio & Landim, Rev. Mod. Phys. 87, 593 (2015) at abstract level
alternative_formulations.caveat: declared class: boundary-driven diffusive lattice gases and their hydrodynamic limits

domain_of_validity.claim: Linear response, Onsager reciprocity, and Green-Kubo apply in the near-equilibrium linear regime around an equilibrium reference state (with field-reversal completion under time-reversal-odd fields); the stochastic-thermodynamics fluctuation relations hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium for the declared stochastic dynamics classes and finite times
domain_of_validity.source: Onsager, Phys. Rev. 37, 405 (1931); Kubo, J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. 12, 570 (1957); Seifert, Phys. Rev. Lett. 95, 040602 (2005) -- all verified 2026-09-23 (APS abstracts / Crossref)
domain_of_validity.caveat: quantum-coherent extensions beyond two-point measurement schemes remain an active edge (also recorded in the sibling record's domain_of_validity)

domain_of_validity.claim: KPZ universality is experimentally established in 1+1 dimensions; higher-dimensional KPZ behavior rests on numerics and lacks an experimental anchor of comparable strength
domain_of_validity.source: Takeuchi & Sano, Phys. Rev. Lett. 104, 230601 (2010) -- APS abstract fetched 2026-09-23 (the 1+1 D anchor); the higher-D statement is the recorded absence of an equivalent anchor, not a cited no-go
domain_of_validity.caveat: the higher-dimensional clause is a boundary statement riding on the verified 1+1 D anchor; if a higher-D experimental anchor exists it upgrades this entry at Stage 2
